title: Reel: the 3-second check we run on every ad
hook: Three things we check before we read a single metric.
caption:
Three things we check before we read a single metric.

1. A face in the first frame.
2. It still works on mute.
3. The product or the problem shows up by second three.

None of these make an ad great. Missing them makes a good ad work harder than it should.

Save this and run the check on your next five ads before they go live.
alt_text: Reel cover in Galvor violet and gold: The 3-second check we run on every ad. Face. Mute. Product. A gold button says Watch the check.

script.setup: Phone on a tripod at eye level, window light, lapel mic. Screen recordings of a public ad from the Meta Ad Library with the brand name and logo blurred (or one of our own demo ads). Edit in CapCut with Galvor violet captions.

scenes.visual: Close-up talking head. A feed scrolls fast on a phone held up to camera.
scenes.voiceover: You get about one swipe to earn the next second. Here's what we check first.

scenes.visual: Screen recording: ad paused on frame one; a gold circle draws around the face.
scenes.voiceover: One. Is there a face in the first frame? People stop for people.

scenes.visual: Same ad with the mute icon highlighted; subtitles pop in.
scenes.voiceover: Two. Can you follow it on mute? Plenty of people scroll with the sound off.

scenes.visual: Timeline scrubber stops at 0:03; product slides into frame.
scenes.voiceover: Three. Is the product or the problem on screen by second three? Or is your hook selling someone else's story?

scenes.visual: Back to talking head, slight push-in.
scenes.voiceover: Miss one and the ad isn't broken. Fix it before you put more money behind it.
scenes.on_screen: Fix it before you scale it

scenes.visual: End card: Galvor logo pill top-left, handle centred.
scenes.voiceover: Follow Galvor for a decode every week.

script.music: Low-key lo-fi or trending instrumental at 10–15% under the voice.
script.notes: Keep cuts every 2–3 seconds. Burn in captions. Blur any brand names in screen recordings.
